migrationid.Closed is keyed by the closing file's name. A set that holds none of those files is held to 1..N with no gap, as a test's crafted set is. So a branch that renamed 0061_pull_request_head_run.up.sql or 0141_drop_broadcast_idempotency_keys.up.sql would lose the boundary. Renaming a migration a database has already recorded is a change no one should make, and I do not count it as a failure.

The README and code comments say Closed is raised only when a forward merge brings a numbered migration main took before this rule reached it. Another open pull request that adds a numbered migration and merges first would need that step here.
Round 7's release-order note (this release before any carrying a timestamped migration), round 4's squash-body note and round 1's `since`-edge note still apply.
